body:
Just to be sure, your database is mysql ? 
Can you see if the format of the column interval (in table mirror) is a string or a integer at this stage of migration ?
Are you migrating from gogs ? If so from which version ?

I suspect that the column format is not yet changed to string. So when the migration script change the value 8 to 8h0m0s it doesn't work. But I am not a expert in xorm and can't setup a similar env to replicate.
The more qualified people will maybe need those information for debug. ^^ 

For reference this is trigger by : go-gitea/gitea#1407
@sapk Yes, i migrated from Gogs, but idk which version have been used in last time. (0.9.~ It`s time when public start thinking about the new fork. I immediately went to Gitea master branch.)
@Lourens-Rich I think this should be caused by #1407 sent by @cez81 . Maybe you can change your custom/conf/app.ini about the mirror sync time interval to a time duration format to resolve this.

I think @sapk is on the right track. The column type might be the problem. In Sqlite which I use the column type is still integer after my change. Don't know if duration is handled differently in Mysql by xorm. The internal Go representation of duration is int64.
@cez81 you are right. XORM will not convert `int` to `bigint` automatically.

This MySQL query should do the trick until there's a proper fix:
```sql
ALTER TABLE mirror MODIFY interval BIGINT;
```

issue.title: Fix broken v27 migration - change mirror interval from int to bigint

issue.body:
Fix for #1496. Migration to v27 didn't alter the column type to bigint (#1407). This fix will alter the column type and set all mirror intervals that are < Mirror.MinInterval to Mirror.DefaultInterval.
Sqlite is ok because uses same integer type.

## Description
Been using `gitea-1.1.0+75-g6a451a2` for a while and today upgraded to `gitea-1.1.0+122-gc764a54` from the [Gitea site](https://dl.gitea.io/gitea/master/), thing is when i want to reach the web UI, nginx shows a 502 error. Inspecting the `gitea-1.1.0+122-gc764a54` image i see the port 3000 is no longer present
```
bash-4.3# netstat -tulpn
Active Internet connections (only servers)
Proto Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address           Foreign Address         State       PID/Program name    
tcp        0      0 0.0.0.0:22              0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      14/sshd
tcp        0      0 127.0.0.11:39612        0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      -
tcp        0      0 :::22                   :::*                    LISTEN      14/sshd
udp        0      0 127.0.0.11:46767        0.0.0.0:*                           -
```

this is the output in the `gitea-1.1.0+75-g6a451a2` image
```
bash-4.3# netstat -tulpn
Active Internet connections (only servers)
Proto Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address           Foreign Address         State       PID/Program name    
tcp        0      0 0.0.0.0:22              0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      14/sshd
tcp        0      0 :::22                   :::*                    LISTEN      14/sshd
tcp        0      0 :::3000                 :::*                    LISTEN      -
```

Is this intended?

One more thing with `gitea-1.1.0+122-gc764a54`, when using the `-h` flag (or any other argument) it panics
```
bash-4.3# /app/gitea/gitea -h
panic: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
